chapterRoutes.title: Departures Drive (upper, elevated) in front of the Main Terminal → "Return to Terminal / Exit" → Airport Expressway north → SR-518 east → I-5 / I-405 junction (Southcenter)

start.note: Upper Departures Drive (layer 2, 2 lanes + kerb lane) at the north end of the terminal frontage, heading SSW past doors; skybridges 6→1 overhead at level 4.

end.note: SR-518 EB splits "Renton (I-405 N)" left / "Tacoma; Portland (I-5 S)" right — chapter waypoint ("drive out").

chapterRoutes.timing: ≈ 5–6 min off-peak (20 mph drives, 30–40 mph expressway, 60 mph SR-518)
chapterRoutes.alt: Shorter (2.5 km) option for spec 10 limits: end at the Airport Expressway → SR-518 merge (s≈3.9 km, lat 47.4631,-122.2879) — "Welcome to Seattle" sign moment, then fade.

streets.name: Departures Drive (upper roadway)
streets.lanes: 2–3 lanes southbound one-way, elevated viaduct (OSM bridge=yes, layer 2) along the terminal face; kerb lane for drop-off at the terminal doors on the right (west); 20 mph.
streets.structure: Concrete viaduct with the terminal's glass curtain wall and canopy on the right, the 7-level garage on the left; six enclosed pedestrian skybridges (OSM "Skybridge 1"–"Skybridge 6", level 4, ~33–40 m long) span overhead between garage and terminal at ~70 m spacing.
streets.signage: Overhead white-on-blue/dark terminal-zone signs listing airlines by door (e.g. "Alaska", "Delta", "United", "Southwest") and door numbers; "Departures" in large letters; kerb signs "Active loading and unloading only" — exact airline-to-door layout changes; verify with current SEA map (gap).
streets.exit: At the south end the drive descends (layer 2→1) and splits: "Return to Terminal / Parking" loop vs "Exit — International Blvd SR 99 / I-5 / I-405 / SR 509" then joins the Airport Expressway northbound via a 1-lane ramp (way 124272635).

streets.name: Arrivals Drive (lower roadway, under Departures)
streets.lanes: 3–5 lanes southbound under the upper drive (maxheight 12'0" = 3.66 m posted), baggage-claim doors on the right; inner islands for shuttles/taxis/TNC (third-floor garage hosts rideshare pickup — verify).
streets.lighting: Dim, under-deck: continuous fluorescent/LED fixtures on the soffit of the upper drive; concrete columns between lanes.

streets.name: Airport Expressway (northbound to SR-518)
streets.lanes: 3 → 4 → 5 lanes, 30 mph near the terminal rising to 40 mph; destination:lanes "Terminal Parking ×3 | Terminal Parking; International Blvd; Rental Car Return; Cell Phone Lot", later "Burien | Burien; Seattle; Tacoma | Seattle; Tacoma" at the SR-518 split.
streets.context: Runs between the garage (west) and the elevated Link 1 Line guideway / SeaTac/Airport station (east, 18 m up); the station's east pedestrian bridge crosses the expressway to International Blvd.

streets.name: SR 518 eastbound — Airport Expressway to I-5/I-405
streets.facts: 3.42-mile freeway Burien–Tukwila; 38,000–102,000 vehicles/day (2011), busiest between the airport and I-5; becomes I-405 east of I-5.
streets.lanes: 3 lanes EB (60 mph), asphalt with concrete bridge decks; at 51st Ave S destination:lanes "Seattle | Renton | Tacoma; Portland; 51st Ave S; Southcenter Pkwy"; final 2-lane split Renton (I-405 N, left) / Tacoma-Portland (I-5 S, right).
streets.context: Link 1 Line elevated guideway parallels the freeway (OSM light_rail bridge layer 3) toward Tukwila Int'l Blvd station; Westfield Southcenter mall to the south-east at the end.

landmarks.name: Sea-Tac Main Terminal (landside face)
facts: Opened 1949; 1973 terminal built around it; central terminal renovated/expanded 2003 by Fentress Architects.
89 gates, Concourses A–D + North/South satellites linked by the SEA Underground people mover.

facade.description: Long low terminal: glass curtain wall and steel canopy on the departures level, concrete lower level; the 2003 Central Terminal is a tall glazed hall facing the airfield (not visible from the drives).

landmarks.name: Sea-Tac parking garage (Port of Seattle)
facts: North America's largest parking structure under one roof (12,100 spaces).
Level 4 connects to the terminal via skybridges 1–6 and to the light-rail station via a 1,200 ft covered walkway.
landmarks.look: Precast concrete decks with horizontal spandrel bands, light grey #a9a8a2, open sides, colour-coded zones

landmarks.name: SeaTac/Airport Link station (1 Line)
facts: Opened 2009-12-19; island platform elevated 60 ft (18 m); steel-truss roof designed by David Hewitt with a flight theme.
West pedestrian bridge to garage level 4; east bridge over the Airport Expressway to International Blvd.

landmarks.name: SeaTac Air Traffic Control Tower (2004)
landmarks.note: Visible landmark north-west of the terminal (47.4557,-122.3014).

landmarks.name: International Arrivals Facility + 780–900 ft aerial walkway (2022)
landmarks.note: Walkway 85 ft above the taxiway; visible from the south end of the drives.

markings.ref: see seattle-bellevue.json markings (WSDOT M-20.10/M-20.30, MUTCD 3D); airport drives: white lane lines, crosswalks at terminal doors, "NO STOPPING" red kerb segments (verify)

trees.note: Landscaping: conifers (Douglas-fir) and deciduous screening along SR-518 and the expressway; lawns/grass medians.

transit.lightRail: 1 Line (Sound Transit Link) on elevated guideway beside the Airport Expressway and SR-518; SeaTac/Airport station 18 m up
transit.bus: RapidRide A Line, ST Express 560, KCM on International Blvd

hotspots.evidence: Port of Seattle: Departures-level peak ~4:30–7:30 a.m.; both drives back up ~11 a.m.–2 p.m.
Port of Seattle: arrivals congested late evening (~20:30 to past midnight).

I-405 corridor Tukwila↔Bellevue severely congested in peaks (e.g. Bellevue→Tukwila ~17:00 up to 97% of days in 2014) and SR-518 carries up to 102,000 veh/day near I-5; queue spill-back onto SR-518 ramps is common (estimate).
